tip_title: You Might Not Need Gap Insurance Anymore. Here's How to Tell.
topic: gap insurance when you need it
blurb:
💡 **Insurance Tip: You Might Not Need Gap Insurance Anymore. Here's How to Tell.**

Gap insurance exists for one specific situation: you owe more on your car loan than the car is currently worth. That's common in the first couple years after you finance a vehicle, because cars depreciate fast and loan balances shrink slowly. But here's the thing most people miss — that gap eventually closes. If you've been paying down your loan for a few years and your car hasn't lost significant value, you might already be past the point where gap coverage is doing anything for you. A quick check: look up your car's current market value (Kelley Blue Book is a common tool), compare it to your loan payoff balance, and if you're no longer underwater, you're probably paying for coverage you don't need.

Not sure how to run the numbers on your specific situation? Your Peachy agent can help you figure out whether gap coverage still makes sense for your vehicle.

📖 [Learn more from Forbes Advisor](https://www.forbes.com/advisor/car-insurance/gap-insurance/)
summary: Covers gap insurance as a periodic review item rather than a purchase decision — specifically, how to check whether you're still upside down on your loan and whether the coverage is still worth keeping.
scoring_notes: Repeat subject of gap insurance, new angle: periodic review of whether you're still underwater on your loan (when to DROP it), vs. the May 8 tip on what gap doesn't cover and the implied prior tip on when to get it. Both audiences skew educated, middle-to-upper income, and have meaningful auto populations. Actionability is high — the Kelley Blue Book check is something anyone can do today. Timeliness is evergreen but scores a 6; no strong seasonal hook. Only trusted-source candidate available after filtering non-approved domains and deduplicating previously covered angles.
